items.q: The board has appointed an independent auditor to ______ how the foundation spends its grant money.
items.vi: Hội đồng đã bổ nhiệm một kiểm toán viên độc lập để giám sát cách quỹ chi tiêu tiền tài trợ.
items.explanation: Oversee = supervise or watch over; the auditor is appointed to check how the foundation spends its money. ✗ overlook — fail to notice, or ignore a fault: the opposite of checking; ✗ overhaul — rebuild or reform completely: an auditor inspects, not reforms; ✗ overdo — do to excess, and it cannot take a how-clause as its object.

items.q: Although they belong to the same party, the two ministers seldom ______ on how tuition fees should be set.
items.vi: Dù cùng một đảng, hai vị bộ trưởng hiếm khi đồng quan điểm về cách ấn định học phí.
items.explanation: See eye to eye (on something) = agree completely; seldom plus on how tuition fees should be set shows disagreement about an issue. ✗ go hand in hand — two things occur together; used of things, not people's opinions; ✗ stand shoulder to shoulder — support one another in a struggle; not about agreeing on a question; ✗ play cat and mouse — toy with or tease someone; no sense of agreement.

items.q: Sociologists describe the rush to buy the latest phone as a form of ______ consumption, a way of displaying wealth rather than meeting a need.
items.vi: Các nhà xã hội học mô tả cơn sốt mua điện thoại đời mới nhất là một dạng tiêu dùng phô trương, một cách khoe của cải hơn là đáp ứng nhu cầu.
items.explanation: Conspicuous consumption is the fixed sociological term for buying expensive goods to show off wealth, which the gloss displaying wealth rather than meeting a need spells out. ✗ obvious — clear, easy to see; not the set phrase; ✗ visible — able to be seen; no collocation with consumption; ✗ noticeable — easy to notice; again not the term.

items.q: ______ the sharp rise in university tuition, enrolment has continued to climb for the fifth year running.
items.vi: Bất chấp học phí đại học tăng mạnh, số sinh viên nhập học vẫn tiếp tục tăng năm thứ năm liên tiếp.
items.explanation: Contrast + noun phrase: the blank is followed by the sharp rise, a noun phrase with no verb, so the preposition despite is needed. ✗ Although — a conjunction that needs a subject and verb (although tuition rose…); ✗ Whereas — also needs a clause, and it contrasts two facts rather than showing an unexpected result; ✗ However — an adverb that links two sentences and cannot govern a noun phrase.

items.q: Parents who do not want their children's test scores shared with private companies may ______ of the scheme by returning a signed form.
items.vi: Phụ huynh không muốn điểm thi của con bị chia sẻ với các công ty tư nhân có thể rút khỏi chương trình bằng cách nộp lại mẫu đơn có chữ ký.
items.explanation: Opt out of = choose not to take part in something; the clue is of the scheme after the blank, which only opt out takes. ✗ rule out — exclude as a possibility; needs a direct object, not of; ✗ leave out — omit, not include; also takes an object, and the parents are not omitting the scheme; ✗ sort out — solve or organise; takes an object and gives no sense of withdrawing.

items.q: The donors ______ have known that the funds were being misused; the accounts were never shown to them.
items.vi: Các nhà tài trợ không thể nào biết được rằng tiền đang bị sử dụng sai mục đích; họ chưa từng được xem sổ sách.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle = it is impossible that something happened; the clue is the accounts were never shown to them, so the donors could not have known. ✗ must have known — near-certainty that they DID know, contradicting the second clause; ✗ should have known — criticises them for failing to know, but the sentence excuses them; ✗ needn't have known — says knowing was unnecessary, which makes no sense.

items.q: Frequent reversals of exam policy ______ public trust in the ministry far more than any single unpopular decision.
items.vi: Việc liên tục đảo ngược chính sách thi cử làm xói mòn lòng tin của công chúng vào bộ nhiều hơn bất kỳ quyết định không được lòng dân nào.
items.explanation: Undermine = gradually weaken; frequent reversals damage public trust, and the comparison with an unpopular decision confirms a harmful effect. ✗ underpin — support or strengthen; the opposite meaning; ✗ underlie — be the hidden cause or basis of; reversals are not the basis of trust; ✗ undergo — experience a process (undergo surgery); trust is not something reversals go through.

items.q: The ministry intends to ______ out printed textbooks ______ 2030, replacing them with tablets in every classroom.
items.vi: Bộ dự định loại bỏ dần sách giáo khoa in trước năm 2030, thay bằng máy tính bảng ở mọi lớp học.
items.explanation: Phase out = withdraw something gradually in stages (replacing them with tablets), and a deadline takes by = no later than 2030. ✗ fade / until — fade out is intransitive (things fade out by themselves) and until marks how long something lasts, not a deadline; ✗ wipe / at — wipe out means destroy completely, and at is not used with a year; ✗ wear / in — wear out means use until unusable; in 2030 is fine but the verb fails.

items.q: ______ should laboratory staff attempt to dispose of chemical waste without wearing protective gloves.
items.vi: Trong bất kỳ trường hợp nào, nhân viên phòng thí nghiệm cũng không được cố xử lý chất thải hóa học mà không đeo găng tay bảo hộ.
items.explanation: Negative-adverbial inversion: the inverted should laboratory staff attempt comes straight after the blank, so the phrase must stand alone, and under no circumstances = never, in no case. ✗ Only after — needs a time noun or clause before the inversion (Only after training should…); ✗ Not until — likewise needs a time phrase or clause (Not until 6 pm should…); ✗ No sooner — needs had + past participle and a following than.

items.q: A: Has the sponsor replied to our proposal yet? B: Not yet. Oh, ______ - here she comes now.
items.vi: A: Nhà tài trợ đã trả lời đề xuất của chúng ta chưa? B: Chưa. Ồ, vừa nhắc đã tới - cô ấy đang đến kìa.
items.explanation: Speak of the devil is said when the person you were just talking about appears; the clue is here she comes now right after mentioning the sponsor. ✗ hold your horses — wait, slow down; not a reaction to someone appearing; ✗ the talk of the town — a noun phrase for something everyone is discussing; cannot stand as an exclamation here; ✗ bite your tongue — stop yourself from saying something; no link to arrival.

items.q: Regulators must ______ a balance between protecting consumers and allowing online retailers to innovate.
items.vi: Các cơ quan quản lý phải tìm được sự cân bằng giữa bảo vệ người tiêu dùng và cho phép các nhà bán lẻ trực tuyến đổi mới.
items.explanation: Strike a balance is the fixed collocation for finding a fair compromise, and between protecting… and allowing… names the two sides being balanced. ✗ hit — reach a level (hit a target) or strike with force; not used with balance; ✗ beat — defeat, or hit repeatedly; no collocation with balance; ✗ knock — hit with a sharp blow; also does not pair with balance.

items.q: In her speech the minister said that the new grading system ______ nationwide the following year.
items.vi: Trong bài phát biểu, bộ trưởng nói rằng hệ thống chấm điểm mới sẽ được áp dụng trên toàn quốc vào năm sau.
items.explanation: Reported speech: after past said that, the minister's original will be introduced backshifts to would be introduced, and the following year (the reported form of next year) confirms the shift. ✗ will be introduced — no backshift after a past reporting verb; ✗ is introduced — present tense, neither backshifted nor future; ✗ had introduced — active, so it needs an object (had introduced what?); the system is introduced, it does not introduce.

items.q: Critics argue that the report ______ the benefits of private tutoring while ignoring the pressure it puts on families.
items.vi: Giới phê bình cho rằng báo cáo thổi phồng lợi ích của việc học thêm trong khi phớt lờ áp lực mà nó gây ra cho các gia đình.
items.explanation: Overstate = describe as bigger or better than it really is; the contrast while ignoring the pressure shows the report exaggerates one side. ✗ overrules — reject a decision using authority (a judge overrules an objection); benefits cannot be overruled; ✗ overrides — cancel or take priority over (override a veto); ✗ overshadows — make something seem less important by comparison; the report is praising the benefits, not eclipsing them.

items.q: The auditor recommended that the foundation ______ its full list of donors public before the next fundraising drive.
items.vi: Kiểm toán viên khuyến nghị quỹ công khai toàn bộ danh sách nhà tài trợ trước đợt gây quỹ tiếp theo.
items.explanation: Subjunctive after a verb of advice: recommended that + subject + base form, so that the foundation make. ✗ makes — third-person -s is the ordinary present, not the subjunctive; ✗ made — past tense; the subjunctive never backshifts, even after past recommended; ✗ will make — no modal is used in the that-clause after recommend.

items.q: We have submitted our final offer for the sponsorship deal, so now ______.
options: the shoe is on the other foot
the ball is in your court
items.answer: the ball is in your court
items.vi: Chúng tôi đã gửi đề nghị cuối cùng cho hợp đồng tài trợ, nên giờ quyền quyết định thuộc về các bạn.
items.explanation: The ball is in your court = it is now your turn to act or decide; the clue is we have submitted our final offer, so now — the next move belongs to the other side. ✗ the shoe is on the other foot — the situation has reversed and the roles have swapped; ✗ the coast is clear — there is no danger of being seen or caught; ✗ the sky is the limit — there is no upper limit to what can be achieved.

items.q: Shoppers who are used to ______ discounts every weekend seldom notice when prices quietly rise.
items.vi: Những người mua sắm đã quen với việc thấy giảm giá mỗi cuối tuần hiếm khi để ý khi giá âm thầm tăng lên.
items.explanation: Be used to + gerund = be accustomed to; are used to (with the verb be) shows the habit meaning, so seeing. ✗ see — the bare infinitive belongs to past-habit used to see, but are before it rules that out; ✗ have seen — a perfect infinitive cannot follow the preposition to here; ✗ being seen — passive: the shoppers do the seeing, they are not seen.

items.q: The plan to fund a library in every rural district did not ______ as hoped, and half the donated money was returned.
items.vi: Kế hoạch tài trợ một thư viện cho mỗi huyện nông thôn đã không thành công như mong đợi, và một nửa số tiền quyên góp bị trả lại.
items.explanation: Pan out = develop or turn out (successfully); did not… as hoped and money was returned show a plan that failed. ✗ pass out — faint, lose consciousness; ✗ hand out — distribute; needs an object (hand out books), and a plan cannot hand out; ✗ peter out — fade away gradually; close in meaning, but it cannot take as hoped — nobody hopes a plan peters out.

items.q: ______ a sudden shortage of nurses, the hospital has begun recruiting from overseas for the first time in its history.
items.vi: Đứng trước tình trạng thiếu y tá đột ngột, bệnh viện lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử đã bắt đầu tuyển dụng từ nước ngoài.
items.explanation: Participle clause: the hospital is the one confronted by the shortage, so the passive participle faced with (= confronted by) opens the sentence; the clue is the with that only the passive form takes. ✗ Facing with — active face takes a direct object with no preposition (facing a shortage); ✗ Having faced with — same error, and the perfect form wrongly puts the shortage before the recruiting; ✗ To face with — an infinitive of purpose makes no sense, and again with is wrong.

items.q: Investing in teacher training rather than new buildings was a ______ decision whose benefits are only now becoming visible.
items.vi: Đầu tư vào đào tạo giáo viên thay vì xây dựng mới là một quyết định có tầm nhìn xa mà lợi ích chỉ giờ đây mới dần lộ rõ.
items.explanation: Far-sighted = showing wise judgement about the future; the clue is benefits are only now becoming visible, i.e. the decision paid off later. ✗ far-flung — distant and widely scattered (far-flung villages); not used of decisions; ✗ far-off — remote in place or time (a far-off land); ✗ far-out — informal for strange or unconventional; the decision is praised, not called odd.

items.q: Every speaker praised the new curriculum, but nobody mentioned ______: the chronic shortage of qualified teachers.
options: the black sheep of the family
items.vi: Diễn giả nào cũng ca ngợi chương trình mới, nhưng không ai nhắc đến vấn đề hiển nhiên mà mọi người đều né tránh: tình trạng thiếu giáo viên có trình độ kéo dài.
items.explanation: The elephant in the room = an obvious problem that everyone avoids discussing; nobody mentioned the chronic shortage although it is plain to all. ✗ the skeleton in the cupboard — a hidden shameful secret; the shortage is public, not secret; ✗ the black sheep of the family — a person who embarrasses the group, not a problem; ✗ the last straw — the final problem that makes a situation unbearable.

items.q: Rival fashion retailers now copy ______ so quickly that a new design rarely stays exclusive for more than a week.
items.vi: Các nhà bán lẻ thời trang đối thủ giờ sao chép lẫn nhau nhanh đến mức một mẫu thiết kế mới hiếm khi giữ được tính độc quyền quá một tuần.
items.explanation: Reciprocal pronoun: rival retailers copy each other's designs, so one another (= each other). ✗ themselves — reflexive: each retailer would copy its own designs, which makes no sense; ✗ each — cannot stand alone as the object of copy (each what?); ✗ another — means a different one, not the mutual action; the pair one another is needed.

items.q: Rather than ______ on the fence any longer, the school board must ______ a clear stance on mobile phones in class.
items.vi: Thay vì tiếp tục lưỡng lự không quyết, hội đồng trường phải có lập trường rõ ràng về điện thoại di động trong lớp.
items.explanation: Sit on the fence = avoid choosing a side (clue: any longer + must… a clear stance), and the verb that collocates with stance is take. ✗ stand / make — stand on the fence is not the idiom, and one does not make a stance; ✗ lean / hold — lean on the fence is literal, and hold a stance is not the standard collocation; ✗ stay / do — stay on the fence is not the idiom and do a stance is impossible.

items.q: Since the scandal broke, the charity's spending has come under ______ scrutiny from journalists and regulators alike.
items.vi: Từ khi vụ bê bối bị phanh phui, chi tiêu của tổ chức từ thiện này đã bị cả nhà báo lẫn cơ quan quản lý xem xét kỹ lưỡng.
items.explanation: Close scrutiny is the standard collocation for very careful examination; come under… scrutiny from journalists and regulators describes intense inspection. ✗ near — close in distance or time only, never in the sense of careful; ✗ tight — pairs with control or security, not scrutiny; ✗ thick — physical thickness (thick fog); no collocation with scrutiny.

items.q: Nobody really expects the cap on private-school fees to survive the next budget, ______?
items.vi: Thật ra chẳng ai mong mức trần học phí trường tư sẽ tồn tại qua kỳ ngân sách tới, phải không?
items.explanation: Question tag after a negative subject: nobody is already negative, so the tag is positive, and the pronoun for nobody is plural they: do they. ✗ don't they — a negative tag after a negative statement; ✗ does it — it would refer to the cap, but the subject of the sentence is nobody; ✗ doesn't it — wrong pronoun and wrong polarity.

items.q: The fund offers full scholarships to ______ students who would otherwise have no chance of attending a specialist high school.
items.vi: Quỹ cấp học bổng toàn phần cho những học sinh có hoàn cảnh khó khăn, những em nếu không sẽ chẳng có cơ hội vào trường chuyên.
items.explanation: Underprivileged = lacking the money and advantages others have; the clue is who would otherwise have no chance — the scholarships help disadvantaged students. ✗ underlying — basic, or hidden beneath the surface (an underlying cause); ✗ understaffed — having too few workers; describes organisations, not students; ✗ undervalued — not appreciated as much as deserved; the sentence is about lack of opportunity, not appreciation.
